topics: Super-mesh analysis and super-node analysis applied to both DC and AC networks containing independent and dependent sources.
Network theorems and applications : Superposition theorem
Millman’s theorem and Maximum power transfer theorem for the analysis of DC and AC networks having independent and dependent sources.
Laplace transforms and transient analysis: Laplace transforms of standard signals and common functions
Transformation of basic signals and circuits to s – domain with and without initial conditions
Transient analysis of RL, RC and RLC networks with DC, impulse, step and sinusoidal inputs
Analysis of low pass and high pass RC circuits using Laplace transforms.
Network functions and two-port parameters: Network functions for single-port and two-port networks
Properties of driving point and transfer functions
Significance of poles and zeros of network functions
Hybrid and Transmission parameters of two-port networks
Reciprocity and symmetry conditions (derivation not required)
Series and parallel connections of two-port networks.

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module. Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks. Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered. Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Analyze electrical networks using mesh and node methods
Apply network theorems to analyze electrical networks
Analyze transient behavior of electrical networks using Laplace transforms
Identify the network functions and parameters of single-port and two-port networks
